h: Bristol climbing: who, when and what next
p: Clip 'n Climb is at its best with a mixed group. Speedy climbers race the timed walls, cautious ones take the balance challenges at their own pace, and everyone gathers round when someone works up the courage for a leap. If you're organising for a gang, put the more confident climbers alongside the nervous ones on side-by-side walls. It keeps things friendly and gives the wobbly ones a bit of moral support.

When to go makes a difference too. Weekends and school holidays are the busy times, so a term-time weekday is the calmer choice if you can swing it. Whenever you go, allow a couple of hours including check-in, harness fitting and the safety briefing. Every climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and there's usually a minimum age for climbers, so check the details when you book.
Eat light beforehand, bring water and leave rings and watches at home. Your forearms will remind you of the session the next morning, which is all part of the charm.

Plenty of Bristol is ready for round two. M Shed on the harbourside tells the story of the city and its people for free, the Aquarium is a short stroll away for a calmer hour, and the Bristol Zoo Project, the city's zoo in its newer home on the northern edge of town, is a big day out in its own right. Cabot Circus is the place if someone in the group insists on shopping.
